reason.description: Why it is forgotten, for example "superseded by lay_out_on_grid".

tools.name: capability_get
tools.description: Fetch a saved capability, including its code. Run it inside run_code: `const cap = await tools.capability_get({ name }); const run = new (Object.getPrototypeOf(async function () {}).constructor)("tools", "args", cap.code); return await run(tools, { ...arguments })`. The program that fetched it counts as one run of it: succeeded when the program ends without an error, failed when it throws.

tools.name: capability_list
tools.description: List the capabilities you saved in earlier tasks, without their code: programs you wrote that combine the robot tools to do something no single tool does. Check it before writing a new program; a capability that fits saves you from solving the problem again. Each has a layer (recipe: skills composed for one kind of task; skill: one reusable operation), a status (verified: it succeeded in several runs; candidate: not yet proven; deprecated: it kept failing, fix it or delete it), what it requires and ensures, and the outcomes of its runs. Verified ones come first, recipes before skills.

tools.name: capability_save
tools.description: Save a program as a named capability of this robot so later tasks can reuse it, or replace an existing one with an improved version (changed code starts a new version as a candidate). Save it after it has worked. Prefer small skills that work on any objects of a kind (spread objects out, turn a flat object face up, find where a piece belongs in a picture, lay objects out on a grid), and a thin recipe that composes them with capability_get. Write the code as the body of an async function of (tools, args) that calls the same tools as your run_code programs, returns its result and throws an Error when it cannot achieve what it ensures. Everything specific to one task belongs in args: saving is refused when the code names objects (e:123) or holds many decimal constants.

layer.description: skill: one reusable operation; recipe: skills composed for one kind of task.

description.description: What it does and what it returns.

requires.description: What must hold in the world before it runs.

ensures.description: What holds in the world after it succeeded.

parameters.description: What each field of args means, for example {"lid": "id of the lid showing the picture"}.

code.description: Body of an async function of (tools, args).

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: ego_annotate
tools.description: Record what you have identified an object to be when the perceived category is wrong or unknown (for example "unknown" for a box or a puzzle piece). Your label replaces its category, and the affordances you name replace the category's defaults, so prediction and planning treat it accordingly: graspable (can be picked), support-surface (things can be put on it), receptacle (things can be put in it), container, pourable (can be carried with its contents and poured), flat.

label.description: Category name to use for it.

tools.name: ego_camera_calibration
tools.description: Read fixed RGB camera intrinsics and camera_to_reference transforms into the middle head_camera frame (OpenCV x right, y down, z forward; translation in metres) without images or motion. Each camera has pixel K and dimensions. No absolute camera pose is provided.

tools.name: ego_candidates
tools.description: Find the objects that could be what the instruction calls something when perception names it differently: the segmenter names things by appearance (a lid printed with a picture can be "picture"), and the classifier only knows the shapes of its categories. Ranks objects by how well their perceived category alternatives, segmenter names and size fit `name` and `size`; without either, lists the objects whose current name is doubtful. Each carries `doubts` and the evidence behind its name. Confirm with ego_inspect or a closer look, then ego_annotate.

name.description: What you are looking for, as a category word, for example "box" or "lid".

size.description: One to three approximate dimensions in metres from the instruction or your expectation.

tools.name: ego_capture_cameras
tools.description: Capture your left, original and right RGB cameras at one sensor timestamp without moving. Saves three JPEG images and a manifest in your workspace and returns their paths, pixel intrinsics K, and fixed camera_to_reference calibration in OpenCV axes, metres, relative to the original head camera. Includes gripper_pose from the same encoder timestamp, with gripper_to_camera transforms for all three views. Works independently of the console camera display mode. No absolute camera poses or synthesized views are provided.

tools.name: ego_explore
tools.description: Turn in place through a full circle to perceive your surroundings. Use it first in a new place or when an object you need is not in ego_state.

timeoutS.description: Maximum seconds to wait for completion (default 120).

tools.name: ego_forget
tools.description: Remove an object from the Ego State as a false perception. Use it only for an object that is physically implausible (marked `unsupported`: floating with nothing under it, or inside another solid object) and that you looked for again, with ego_observe from a place where its spot is in view, without perceiving it (its lastSeenAgoS keeps growing). The robot refuses an object it holds or perceived in the last few seconds.

reason.description: Why it is implausible and how you looked for it again.

tools.name: ego_gripper_pose
tools.description: Read your gripper-link pose relative to your base and the robot cameras from current joint encoders, your body model and fixed camera calibration. No motion or image capture. gripper_to_camera maps gripper-local points (x forward, y left, z up) into each OpenCV camera frame (x right, y down, z forward), translations in metres. The gripper frame is the gripper link origin. Includes sensor timestamp, measured lift/reach and gripper_to_base. For a pose synchronized to images, use ego_capture_cameras and its embedded gripper_pose instead of combining separate calls.

tools.name: ego_inspect
tools.description: Look closely at the top face of an object with one fresh frame of each camera, read from the camera that sees most of it: its colours on a px x px grid. rows is in the object's own frame (row 0 is its +y edge, column 0 its -x edge, as seen from above with its heading yawDeg). worldRows is the same face as seen from above with the map's +y up and +x to the right: rows turned worldTurnDeg counter-clockwise (yawDeg rounded to a quarter turn), so faces of objects lying at different headings compare directly in worldRows. Putting an object down with place yaw = its current yawDeg + k x 90 degrees (given in radians) turns its face k quarter turns counter-clockwise as seen from above. Each cell is [r, g, b] or null where the face is out of view or hidden. Stand within about a metre with the object in front of you. You have two cameras on your head: head_camera looks ahead and sees a surface only from some way ahead of it; wide_camera, a short-focal-length camera tilted further down, also sees the strip of a table next to the edge you stand at and the gripper at work, in less detail. When part of the face is unseen, hint says why (too close below the view, beside or behind it, too far, hidden) and how to move. Use it to compare printed or patterned faces, read which side of a flat object is up, or tell similar objects apart. A printed flat object lying with its plain back up: use plain === true or interiorColors (under about 20). Do not use spread / interiorSpread alone — table lighting makes cardboard look variegated in RGB even when it is one colour. Turn it over (place with flip) and look again. Flat objects lying on or against each other hide parts of their faces and can be perceived as one object, and one lying on another can hide it wholly: set them apart on free space first, looking again where each one lay after picking it up. The object frame stays fixed to the object between views and while it is carried, so one inspection before picking it tells which place yaw turns its face as you want.

entity.description: Id of the object to inspect.

px.description: Grid size, 4 to 128 (default 24). Raise it when sourcePx is large and you need pattern detail.

tools.name: ego_match_face
tools.description: Find where the top faces of objects appear on the top face of a reference object printed at the same scale (puzzle pieces on the picture of their box, tiles on a pattern sheet). It works from the faces you remember: the robot remembers the top face of every object up to about 0.6 m that it sees within 1.5 m (ego_state appearance says how much and how long ago), and refreshes the ones in view first; a face put down since it was last seen must be looked at again. Match all objects of a task in one call. For each it compares the colours of every placement and quarter turn and returns the best few: offsetM is where the face centre belongs on the reference, in the reference frame from its centre; turnDeg is how far the face must turn counter-clockwise to line up with the reference; placeYawDeg is the heading (degrees; place takes radians) that lines it up with the reference as the reference lies now. To build the picture elsewhere at heading H, put each object at centre + offsetM turned by H, with place yaw = H + turnDeg. score is a correlation (1 = identical); a best score barely above the second is ambiguous, so look closer (raise px toward 32) and match again. offsetM is good to about one cell (cellM): when you know the layout (for example a grid of equal pieces), snap it to the nearest slot. plain / interiorColors (under about 20) means a cardboard back facing up; do not trust spread alone. An entry with error says what to look at.

entities.description: Ids of the objects whose faces are sought.

reference.description: Id of the object showing the whole picture.

px.description: Cells across each object's shorter side, 4 to 32 (default 24).

tools.name: ego_observe
tools.description: Report what your two cameras detect right now (categories, distances, which camera, and screwHoles on parts that show mating holes). Your world model also updates continuously; use ego_state for the accumulated picture, including screwHoles once a detection has been fused.

tools.name: ego_predict
tools.description: Predict the consequences of a skill before doing it. Returns a receipt with a risk score, the issues found (for example a target whose position is too uncertain to grasp reliably), and the planned motion. Skills: "navigate" (needs x, y, optional yaw in radians), "pick" (needs target; a pourable container is picked with what lies in it once nothing lies on top of it), "place" (needs on: a surface, a part that has screw holes to mate onto, an open drawer to put the object into, or a larger bowl to nest a bowl in; optional offset; or at: [x, y] to put it down on the floor; when the held part and the mate both have screw holes, place seats those holes (on the mate itself, or on a surface with alignTo naming the mate; optional hole picks which mate hole / family, e.g. "wing" or "wheel_0"; alignHoles: false keeps a manual offset); optional roll in radians tips it about the arm before release, e.g. π/2 = 90° to set a flat object down on its side; not together with flip), "pour" (the held object must be pourable; needs on: a surface; tips it over the spot so its contents slide out there in a heap, then holds it upright again, still in the gripper; the spot keeps the contents' slide from every edge so nothing falls off; count the contents before pouring, since flat ones can land wholly hidden under one another), "open" / "close" (needs target: a drawer; the robot pulls or pushes its handle and ends standing back so the inside is in view). Objects lying on the floor, such as chairs or a dropped flat piece, are picked from beside them; look at one first from where it is in view (ego_inspect's hint says how far back), since docked beside it the cameras no longer see it. Small ones are lifted clear and carried like objects taken off a table; large ones are carried a few centimetres above the floor in front of the robot, and put down with at; while carrying them the robot needs more room to turn. Objects inside a drawer are only seen while it is open. If the risk is too high or the skill is infeasible, follow the issues (for example move closer and observe, or choose another spot) and predict again. An infeasible receipt lists blockers: entities in the way, whether they can be moved, and parking spots (parkAt) out of the way; clear a movable blocker first (pick it, place it at a parking spot), then predict the original skill again. A receipt can be run once and expires.

target.description: pick: id of the object to grasp; open/close: id of the drawer.

on.description: place: id of the surface, screw-hole part, open drawer or larger bowl to put the held object on or in; pour: id of the surface.

offset.description: place, pour: [dx, dy] of the spot from the surface centre in the surface frame, metres; without it the free spot nearest you. If something already lies at the requested spot, the free spot nearest it is used instead and the issues say where (the receipt plan.spot holds the spot used). Ignored when screw holes are aligned.

alignTo.description: place: id of the part whose screw holes the held part should seat on. Use when on is a table or other surface and the mate is another object on it; omit when on itself is the mate.

hole.description: place: which screw hole (or family) on the mate to seat, e.g. "wing_0", "wing", "gear", "wheel_2". Without it, multi-hole parts pick the matching family; a single hub picks the nearest mount.

alignHoles.description: place: seat screw holes when both parts have them (default true when on is the mate or alignTo is set). Set false to keep a manual offset.

at.description: place on the floor: [x, y] in metres.

yaw.description: navigate: goal heading; place: final heading of the object's frame (as ego_state yawDeg and ego_inspect report it), radians; the wrist turns it.

flip.description: place: turn the held object upside down before setting it down. pick: take it so that it can be turned over later; some arms take it tilted for that, and a place with flip says when the object must be picked again with flip.

roll.description: place: tip the held object about the arm before setting it down, radians (π/2 = 90° onto its side). Not together with flip.

clearance.description: place, pour: least gap in metres kept to objects already on the surface (default 0.015). With an offset, 0 allows contact or overlap (interlocking pieces, stacking): the spot is used exactly as requested, never shifted aside. Screw-hole alignment always uses 0.

tools.name: ego_query
tools.description: Find perceived objects by category (for example "cup", "table") and/or near another object. Matching uses each object's role (the scene-level reading of what it is) and then its category probabilities, best match first, so a sideboard partly seen and labelled "counter" is still found.

category.description: Object category or role to look for.

near.description: Id of an object whose surroundings to search, for example "e:3".

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_start
tools.description: Start background RGB recording at a simulation-clock FPS. Records only head_camera. with same-timestamp measured odometry, encoders and calibration. Does not move the robot. Start before issuing navigation with skill_run wait=false; let this recorder sample independently of model/tool latency, then stop after navigation completes. Do not approximate 2 FPS by repeatedly calling ego_capture_cameras. Recording stops at max_frames or fails visibly on missed samples.

max_frames.description: Recording frame bound, default 256; provider bounds apply.

request_key.description: Stable 8–128 character recording-start key; reuse after lost responses.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_status
tools.description: Inspect recording status, actual sensor counts, simulation timestamps and errors. Does not command motion.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_stop
tools.description: Stop sampling and finalize all queued RGB evidence from the selected recording cameras; cancel=true explicitly discards the recording. If status is finalizing, query status until terminal. Does not stop or start robot motion.

cancel.description: Default false: preserve evidence. True cancels recording.

tools.name: ego_state
tools.description: Read your current understanding of the world: your own position, what you are holding, the skill in progress, and every object you have perceived with its estimated position, position uncertainty in metres, size, what it rests on, and when you last saw it. Objects you have not seen are absent, and positions are estimates. screwHoles lists mating screw holes on a part (id and body-frame p in metres; source observed when a camera saw them, else prior from the category); use them with place alignTo / hole. appearance says what you remember of an object's top face: how long ago you saw it, the share seen, plain / interiorColors (plain true or interiorColors under about 20: a cardboard back; do not use spread alone — lighting makes a plain back look varied) and stale (put down since, look again); ego_match_face compares remembered faces.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: reflect
tools.description: Reflect before trying again when the task is not progressing although no tool failed: a result does not match the goal, something expected is missing, or the same approach keeps falling short. Describe the difficulty; returns the operator's messages, earlier failures, the robot's evidence on the objects involved and, for a deep reflection, a digest of the scene, then the questions to answer before the next step. Print the returned text and answer it after the program ends.

difficulty.description: What is going wrong, with the observations that show it.

name.description: The object the instruction means, as a category word, when one is involved.

size.description: Its approximate dimensions in metres, if known.

depth.description: shallow: a quick check of one step; deep (default): question the understanding of the task, the assumptions and the method.

tools.name: report_problem
tools.description: Alert the operator that you hit a situation you cannot resolve by yourself: an unexpected error, a skill that keeps failing, or a task that cannot be done from here. Before calling, review your own tool calls in this turn and diagnose: which prediction or skill failed, the error text, how often it repeated, where you were, and how it relates to blockers, uncertainty, or missing or duplicate objects in the ego state. The operator console shows the report as an alert. Call it once, then stop.

goal.description: What you are trying to achieve.

step.description: The step you were carrying out when you got stuck.

diagnosis.description: The cause you diagnosed from your tool log and the evidence for it.

message.description: What happened, what you tried, and what you need from the operator.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: skill_run
tools.description: Execute the plan of a receipt from ego_predict. Waits for the skill to finish unless wait is false. For place, waiting includes bounded post-release observation. state=succeeded means mechanical execution completed: inspect verification separately. A failed or unknown verification must be resolved before continuing dependent placements; use the measured errors to re-plan, or inspect from a better view. The runtime never retries a placement automatically. The robot refuses receipts that are infeasible, expired, already used, or above the risk limit.

tools.name: skill_status
tools.description: Read the state of a running or finished skill.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

content.text: Mechanical execution completed and fresh stable observations passed placement verification within the reported contact-height tolerance.

texts: Mechanical execution completed and fresh stable observations passed placement verification within the reported contact-height tolerance.

block.text: Mechanical execution completed and fresh stable observations passed placement verification within the reported contact-height tolerance.
